description: Go CLI that streams a ~1GB ad CSV, aggregates per campaign, writes top-10 CTR / CPA CSVs.

features.title: CLI skeleton
features.description: go.mod, cmd/aggregator with --input and --output flags. Exit 0 on success, 1 on I/O fault, 2 on usage error. A missing input file gives exit 1 and a clear stderr message. The output dir is created if absent. init.sh gates go live.
features.evidence: Gates (CI_SINCE=false): bash init.sh exit 0 — jq lint, gofmt, go vet, go test -race (TestRun 9/9 subtests), go build; gate [5] PENDING until agg/stream-parse adds testdata/golden. Runtime (built bin/aggregator, WSL): AC "Runnable via CLI": `--input in.csv --output out/nested` -> exit 0, nested dir created, no output; `-h` -> exit 0, usage on stdout; `--input in.csv` -> exit 2 "aggregator: --output is required" + usage on stderr; `--bogus` -> exit 2 "flag provided but not defined: -bogus". AC "Handle missing files gracefully": `--input nope.csv` -> exit 1 "aggregator: cannot read input: open .../nope.csv: no such file or directory"; input is a directory -> exit 1 "cannot read input: ... is a directory".

features.title: Streaming CSV parse + malformed rows
features.description: Read the CSV row by row; memory must not grow with file size. Validate the header. A row is malformed if it has the wrong field count, an empty campaign_id, a date that is not YYYY-MM-DD, a non-integer or negative impressions/clicks/conversions, or a spend that is not a decimal or is negative. Malformed rows are skipped and counted; the count goes to stderr. Every malformed row is also written to <output>/malformed_rows.csv (line_number,reason,raw_line).
acceptance: Malformed rows written to a file (owner, 2026-11-21)
features.evidence: Gates (CI_SINCE=false): bash init.sh exit 0 — jq lint, gofmt, vet, go test -race (ingest: TestParseRecord 21 cases, TestParseStream, TestParseHeaderErrors, TestParseStopsOnMalformedHandlerError, TestParseRecordDoesNotAllocate, MalformedLog tests; cli: 11 cases), build, gate [5] now live: bin/aggregator on testdata/sample.csv == testdata/golden/malformed_rows.csv. Runtime: `bin/aggregator --input testdata/sample.csv --output $T` -> exit 0, stderr "aggregator: 7 rows processed, 6 malformed rows skipped (see $T/malformed_rows.csv)". AC "Handle malformed rows gracefully" + "Malformed rows written to a file": malformed_rows.csv lists lines 8 invalid date, 9 "expected 6 fields, got 5", 10 empty line, 11 invalid clicks, 12 empty campaign_id, 13 invalid spend (line_number,reason,raw_line). AC "Memory-efficient on ~1GB": real ad_data.csv (CRLF) -> exit 0, "26843544 rows processed, 0 malformed rows skipped", wall 3.67s, max RSS 2048 KB (/usr/bin/time -v); BenchmarkParse 329 MB/s, 2 allocs per Parse call, 0 per row (AllocsPerRun test). Empty input / wrong header -> exit 1 (cli tests).

features.title: Per-campaign aggregation
features.description: For each campaign_id compute total_impressions, total_clicks, total_spend (summed as int64 cents), total_conversions, CTR = clicks/impressions (0 when impressions = 0), and CPA = spend/conversions (null when conversions = 0).
acceptance: Aggregate by campaign_id: totals, CTR, CPA (null if conversions = 0)
Correct results, matching expected values precisely
features.evidence: Gates (CI_SINCE=false): bash init.sh exit 0 — jq lint, gofmt, vet, go test -race (agg: TestAggregateSample, TestAddCopiesCampaignID, TestAddDoesNotAllocateForKnownCampaign, TestDerivedMetrics 3 cases; cli: 12 cases), build, gate [5] golden diff. AC "Aggregate by campaign_id: totals, CTR, CPA (null if conversions = 0)": TestAggregateSample sums testdata/sample.csv to CMP001 26000/640/9370c/27 … CMP004 9000/90/2000c/0 (hand-computed); TestDerivedMetrics: brief row CTR 0.05 CPA 20.0008, zero conversions -> CPA ok=false, zero impressions -> CTR 0. features.title: Parallel parse
features.description: Parse the input on N worker goroutines (default: all CPUs, --workers to override). A reader cuts the stream into fixed-size chunks on line boundaries from a bounded buffer pool; each worker folds rows into its own accumulator; the partial aggregates are merged at the end. Malformed rows keep exact physical line numbers and file order. Outputs must be byte-identical to the single-threaded run; memory stays bounded by the pool. Re-run the benchmark and update README numbers and results/.
acceptance: Outputs identical to the single-threaded run
Malformed rows keep exact line numbers and order
features.evidence: Gates (CI_SINCE=false): bash init.sh exit 0 — gofmt, vet, go test -race (new: TestParseWorkersAgree 9 subtests = workers 1/2/8 x chunk 256/300/4096 on a generated 3000-line file mixing valid rows, every malformed kind, LF/CRLF, lines between maxLine and chunk and longer than a chunk, last line over-long without terminator — stats, malformed rows incl. line numbers and totals identical to the single-worker run; TestParseStopsOnMalformedHandlerError stops at the 3rd callback and drains without deadlock; TestParseHeaderOnly; TestMerge; cli --workers 0 -> exit 2, --workers 3 on sample -> exit 0), `go test -race -count=3 ./internal/ingest` clean, build, gate [5] golden diff with --workers 1 and --workers $(nproc).
